html:
In July 1915 United States Marines landed in Haiti after a mob killed President Vilbrun Guillaume Sam, and they stayed until 1934. Washington wanted to protect American banks and keep Germany out of the Caribbean.

The Americans controlled Haiti's customs and finances. They built roads using forced labour, the corvee, and pushed through a constitution that let foreigners own land. Peasant fighters, the Cacos, rose against them; their leader Charlemagne Peralte was killed in 1919, and thousands of Haitians died in the war.

The occupation left a centralised state and a new army, the Garde d'Haiti, which later backed Duvalier. The US occupied the Dominican Republic next door at the same time, part of the era of banana wars.
